scope: Verify a low-bandwidth, spatially queryable national river-network source for freshwater scope discovery; not a species-occurrence or regional inventory review.

dataset.title: Rivers (Global - edition 2026)
dataset.license: CC BY 4.0 per FAO catalog; the source HydroRIVERS dataset refers to the separate HydroSHEDS v1 license agreement.
dataset.lineage: The FAO 2026 rivers layer is derived from HydroRIVERS/HydroSHEDS and adds a perennial/intermittent flow-regime classification described as derived from HydroATLAS indicators.
dataset.sourceResolution: HydroRIVERS source layers are based on a 15 arc-second DEM.
dataset.sourceNetworkThreshold: Catchment area at least 10 km2 or average river flow at least 0.1 m3/s, or both.

decision.use: Use the WFS for targeted research queries by a known region or waterbody envelope, then validate named rivers and geometry against current local sources before any regional assignment.
limitations: The bbox sample is not a Cavite boundary or Cavite-only count; the rectangle spans neighboring land and water.
The network represents modeled reaches and can omit smaller streams below its stated catchment/flow threshold.
A 15-arc-second source resolution is useful for screening major waterways but does not establish local channel centerlines or positional accuracy.
The available layer does not establish fish occurrence, present conditions, accessibility, legal catchability, or water safety.
The FAO catalog's CC BY 4.0 statement and the underlying HydroSHEDS v1 license must both be reviewed before publishing geometry or derived layers.
The flow-classification field names were observed, but their class meanings have not yet been checked against the technical report.
next: Review the FAO HydRiver technical report and HydroSHEDS v1 license against the intended use before retaining or publishing any subset.
Choose a rights-cleared current province/region AOI or use an explicitly labeled bounding-box search with no administrative claims.
Query a small, bounded study area; save the source response in ignored research storage with retrieval time and a SHA-256 receipt.
Compare returned reaches and names against official or locally validated waterway references, then document omissions and positional limits.
Keep species evidence in separate, site-linked source records.
